claim: finite context and kernel properties under which the corresponding learners succeed
issue: KY2017 characterizes success by the very weak properties, with the rank and witness-cardinality parameters and membership queries (l.123–126, 448–453). The generic names can be mistaken for the strong properties.
suggested_fix: Kanazawa and Yoshinaka (2017) characterized learners' success with membership queries by very weak finite context and kernel properties.

claim: exactly n levels on every branch
issue: The family is over one leaf symbol and counts constructors, not vertices including the leaf. This matters for the uniqueness of the deleted unmarked word (l.159–179, 681–694).
suggested_fix: Consider an abstract licensing condition: structures over one leaf symbol, built by binary combination and unary marking with exactly $n$ constructors on every branch, must contain a mark.

claim: the product of the three quantities ... tight up to a factor O(n)
issue: The lengths are maxima, and the exemplar factor is max(kappa,1). The lower bound holds for every presentation; tightness is an existential upper bound, not an upper bound on all presentations. C01 improved but not fully explicit (l.189–196, 889–899).
suggested_fix: An untyped frame grammar has $n+1$ nonterminals, one frame of length at most $2n$ per nonterminal, and right-hand sides of length at most $3n$, but exponentially many productions. For every exemplar presentation, the product of nonterminal count, maximal right-hand-side length and the greater of one and the maximal exemplar length has an exponential lower bound, attainable within a factor $O(n)$.

claim: Hence specific learners need exponentially much data
issue: The primal and Rec lower bounds follow from Theorem A(ii); the dual result does not. The sentence also does not identify total data length rather than the number of examples (l.925–928, 970–1061).
suggested_fix: Specific reconstruction and learning algorithms also require data of exponential total length.

claim: total length ... under any observer; ... a marked leaf from an unmarked pair of leaves
issue: Theorem C(iii) covers untyped presentations explicitly; C(iv) compares specific bracketed strings, not arbitrary marked expressions or bare juxtaposed leaves. Lower bounds are not matching upper bounds for all presentations.
suggested_fix: Counting all productions and witnesses, a two-valued observer recording mark presence permits a frame presentation of total length $O(n^2)$; every exemplar presentation has at least exponential total length, typed or untyped. Frames likewise have exponential total-length lower bounds without an observer separating a unary-marked leaf from the binary combination of two unmarked leaves.

claim: Q^{r,s} keeps a representative of each quotient
issue: The range is quotients represented in the fixed J, not all quotients of M_n. The source defines Q^{r,s}(J_i,E_i); at the stabilized stage i the eventual atom belongs to N_i because N_j=N_i, even if E_i is not yet exhaustive. The argument is valid but that transfer is implicit.
suggested_fix: The argument carries over to Algorithm~3 of \citet{kanazawa2023wollic} ($\cap$ available, rank $r\ge2$, terminal-block bound $s\ge1$). After stabilisation at stage $i$, $J$ is fixed; once $E$ exhausts $\Sub(M_n)$, $Q^{r,s}(J,E)$ represents every quotient of a context in $J$. Thus the stable grammar $G_i$ contains an atom $e$ denoting $L(G_n,E_{n-1})$, and the absent rule $(\eps,\eps)^\lhd\to\Lfl e\,e\Rfl$ must fail the test on $E_i$, requiring $w^*_{n-1}\in E_i$.

claim: with this word as the initial set covering the atoms
issue: The preceding one-word witness is the natural antecedent, so the substantive restriction in C09 is fixed. A word is not a set; explicitly choose its singleton and the initial data to be that singleton. The claim is not a negation of the existential (d†′) for all D.
suggested_fix: Let $d$ be such a word. With initial data $D=\{d\}$, the additional examples in (d$^{\dagger\prime}$), which bounds their number, cannot all have length polynomial in the size of the target grammar.

claim: rank 2; apply the proof relative to L
issue: The substantive epsilon repair is sound; rank at most 2 and the empty-language case can be stated explicitly. The empty-language case is vacuous for positive presentations.
suggested_fix: Every language of $\bigcup_s\Ccf s$ has a CFG of rank at most $2$ with the very weak $1$-FKP (\citealp[Prop.~9.7]{kuriyama-tcs1} with \citealp[Sec.~6.3]{yoshinaka2015}; directly, for $L=\emptyset$ take $I=\emptyset$; otherwise apply the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:rec-kernel} relative to $L$ to a characteristic sample of $L\setminus\{\eps\}$ (if nonempty) and, if $\eps\in L$, add an initial $A\to\eps$ with kernel $\{\eps\}$).

issue: The conclusion correctly separates the proof routes, but should use the exact factor max(kappa,1) for notational consistency and explicitly include the untyped case in total-length lower bounds. For M_n, kappa>=1 follows from soundness, so omission is not a counterexample.
